raw_meta_yaml:
# XIOS -- XML-IO-SERVER, the asynchronous parallel I/O server used by a number of
# climate models: the model declares its output in XML, and dedicated server
# processes do the writing. Consumers link `-lxios` and compile against its
# Fortran modules.
#
# XIOS has no CMake or autotools build. It is built by FCM (a Perl build system)
# via ./make_xios, configured by three hand-written "arch" files --
# arch-<NAME>.{env,path,fcm}. build.sh generates an arch-CONDA triplet pointing
# at $PREFIX, as other packagings of XIOS do for their own targets.
#
# VERSION: upstream migrated from SVN to git, and the revision consumers pin is
# SVN r2701 -- commit 2eb572f on the XIOS2 branch. Upstream publishes no release
# tag for it, so the version string spells out what it is: XIOS 2, r2701.
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "2.2701"
  commit: 2eb572f0986eca19031eb6c294d116646010687c

package:
  name: xios
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://gitlab.in2p3.fr/ipsl/projets/xios-projects/xios/-/archive/${{ commit }}/xios-${{ commit }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 1260933df79937f571aa2dd5edaead8f1288409a0d2d49d879af552d84dc7594
  patches:
    # r2701 restored most of the STL includes older revisions dropped, but
    # extern/remap's vendored earcut.hpp still comments out <tuple> and
    # <cstddef> while using std::tuple_element / std::get / std::size_t, which
    # current libstdc++ no longer exposes transitively.
    - patches/0001-earcut-standard-headers.patch

build:
  number: 0
  # MPI-variant build string, per conda-forge convention for MPI-linked packages.
  string: mpi_${{ mpi }}_${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
  # mpich/openmpi are not built for win-64 on conda-forge, and the FCM build
  # (./make_xios) is a Unix-only build system besides.
  skip:
    - win

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - make
    # FCM is Perl, and its extract/build stages use URI.
    - perl
    - perl-uri
  host:
    - ${{ mpi }}
    - libnetcdf * mpi_${{ mpi }}_*
    - netcdf-fortran * mpi_${{ mpi }}_*
    - hdf5 * mpi_${{ mpi }}_*
    # Headers only: XIOS includes boost but links no boost_* library (its
    # %BASE_LD adds -L for boost yet never a -l). libboost-devel would pull the
    # compiled libboost into the runtime closure for nothing -- rattler-build
    # flags it as "Overdepending against libboost". libboost-headers has no
    # run_exports, so the run requirement below is spelled out by hand.
    - libboost-headers
    - blitzpp
  run:
    - ${{ mpi }}
    # The installed headers include boost: xios_spl.hpp -- which practically
    # every other XIOS header pulls in -- includes <boost/unordered_map.hpp>,
    # among others. Anything compiling against XIOS therefore needs the boost
    # headers present, and nothing else in the closure puts them there.
    - libboost-headers

tests:
  - package_contents:
      include:
        - xios.mod
      bin:
        - xios_server.exe
      # XIOS produces a STATIC library, so this is a plain file glob rather than
      # the `lib:` matcher (which looks for a shared object).
      files:
        - lib/libxios.a
  - script:
      - bash test_xios.sh
    files:
      recipe:
        - test_xios.sh

about:
  # The old Trac forge at forge.ipsl.jussieu.fr is gone (it no longer answers at
  # all), and upstream's public presence is now the GitLab Pages site below.
  homepage: https://ipsl.pages.in2p3.fr/projets/xios-projects/xios/
  repository: https://gitlab.in2p3.fr/ipsl/projets/xios-projects/xios
  documentation: https://ipsl.pages.in2p3.fr/projets/xios-projects/xios/XIOS_user_guide/
  summary: XML-IO-SERVER, parallel I/O management for climate models
  description: |
    XIOS manages the I/O of climate models. It lets a model describe its output
    declaratively in XML and offloads the writing to dedicated server processes,
    so that diagnostic output is asynchronous and does not stall computation.
  # XIOS itself is CeCILL v2 (SPDX capitalises it as CECILL; upstream ships it
  # as Licence_CeCILL_V2). Three third-party components are vendored in the
  # tarball and end up inside libxios.a and the installed headers, so their
  # licences are part of what this package distributes:
  #   Clipper 6.2.9, extern/remap/src/clipper.{hpp,cpp}   BSL-1.0
  #   Mapbox earcut.hpp, extern/remap/src/earcut.hpp      ISC
  #   RapidXML, tools/archive/rapidxml.tar.gz             BSL-1.0 OR MIT
  # RapidXML's own licence.txt offers Boost or MIT; BSL-1.0 is taken here, so
  # the expression collapses to one BSL-1.0 term. Neither Clipper nor earcut
  # ships a licence file upstream, hence the two LICENSE.* files in the recipe.
  license: CECILL-2.0 AND BSL-1.0 AND ISC
  license_file:
    - Licence.txt
    - Licence_CeCILL_V2-en.txt
    - extern/rapidxml/include/license.txt
    - LICENSE.clipper
    - LICENSE.earcut

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - ickc
